title: Eventual smoothness for an affine source chart
statement: Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category, $X:I\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a diagram with affine transition morphisms and Noetherian quasi-separated stages [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $\alpha:S\to X$ a limiting cone. Fix $i\in I$ and an affine scheme $P$ with a locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism $p:P\to X_i$. If the canonical second projection $P\times_{X_i}S\to S$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], then for some arrow $j\to i$ the second projection $P\times_{X_i}X_j\to X_j$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, affine-source part of the affine-local reduction; Situation 081D; Tags 0CAQ and 01ZM(2)-(3)

proof.text: Take a finite affine cover B of the Noetherian base X_i. Pull it back to P, then take a finite affine cover of every pulled-back piece; quasi-compactness of p makes these pieces compact. Binding these covers gives a finite affine source cover U. Each chart map factors as a:U_k to B_l followed by the base open immersion. Pullback pasting and cancellation of the open immersion identify smoothness of the limit chart over the preimage of B_l.

For each source chart base change the diagram X to the corresponding affine base chart B_l over Over i. Every object of this diagram is affine because the transitions of X are affine. Its canonical cone is limiting. Apply affine-diagram smoothness descent to a and the projection maps to B_l. Compose with the open immersion to get eventual smoothness of the source chart over X_j.

Cofilteredness of Over i gives a common index below the finitely many chart stages, including for an empty cover. Pullback pasting and stability under base change transfer chart smoothness to that index. The pulled-back chart cover covers the new model, and source locality of smoothness proves the desired second projection smooth.

mathlib_searches.results: Smooth finite presentation and standard-smooth chart declarations only; no eventual smoothness theorem. Remote search uses newer IsSmooth names; pinned Mathlib uses Smooth.
Smooth composition and base-change instances; no eventual smoothness theorem.

Mathlib LocalFlatDescent and Etale.Descent require faithfully flat base change, absent here. The source library has no eventual smoothness theorem. The NoetherianApproximation theorem is restricted to finite-type-over-Z stages. Blueprint searches for 0C0C and affine smooth limit returned no duplicates.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_stage_of_affine_source_limit {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I]
    [IsCofiltered I] {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (X : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (α : (Functor.const I).obj S ⟶ X)
    (hα : IsLimit (Cone.mk S α))
    (hXa : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (X.map f))
    (hN : ∀ i, IsNoetherian (X.obj i))
    (hqs : ∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (X.obj i))
    {i : I} {P : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine P] (p : P ⟶ X.obj i)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    [Smooth (pullback.snd p (α.app i))] :
    ∃ j : Over i, Smooth (pullback.snd p (X.map j.hom))
